To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) response suppression during the signal is nearly complete, (2) response suppression during intertrial intervals varies as a function of relative signal duration, absolute shock rate, and shock-correlated and non-shock-correlated stimulus relations, and (3) the patterning of responding between successive shocks is affected by both relative signal duration, which covaries with absolute shock rate, as well as shock-correlated and shock-correlated stimulus relations.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the intertrial interval as a stimulus, and with the effects of that stimulus on the patterning of responding during a signal and between successive shocks.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative delay to reinforcement is a critical variable in the control of conditioned suppression.

the effects of relative signal and intertrial-intensity duration on response suppression during conditioned suppression are consistent with the effects on conditioned suppression reported for autoshaping.
the relative durations of signal and intertrial interval are important variables in conditioned suppression, but the precise nature of that importance remains to be elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the conditioned suppression paradigm, the intertrial interval functions as a stimulus that can be conditioned to suppress behavior.
the effects of relative conditioned stimulus and inter-trial interval on suppression are comparable to the effects of relative delay to reinforcement on autoshaping.
, in the conditioned-suppression procedure, intertrial-intervall stimuli are not simply "background stimuli," but rather are stimuli with which the subject has an ongoing relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the intertrial interval should be treated as a stimulus, rather than a nonstimulus, and that the effects of relative conditioned stimulus and inter-trial interval durations on conditioned suppression are consistent with an analysis based upon the relative delay to reinforcement.
the relative duration of the signal and intertrial interval can have important effects on behavior in conditioned suppression.
the relative delay to reinforcement metric is a useful tool for analyzing the effects of experimental manipulations that vary the relative delay to shock and the intertrial-interval duration.
